scope: search_archive_model_small; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Unknown outcomes are classified as retryable-unavailable for archive transport
findings.issue: A post-send StorageError/JSON/timeout after the HTTP body has begun (e.g. response validation failure) is caught by the generic `except Exception` at line 40 and re-raised as ArchiveSynthesisTransportUnavailable, but `ScopedModelClient.complete_with_receipt` only converts errors to LLMOutcomeUnknown when it wraps transport internally. Here `client.complete_with_receipt` already raises LLMOutcomeUnknown for unknowns (line 39 handles that correctly), but other exceptions that occur after `http_attempted=True` inside model.py's transport are already converted to LLMOutcomeUnknown before leaving the client, so line 40 in practice only sees pre-HTTP/local failures - acceptable. However, if `ArchiveSynthesisReceipt` construction or the final return raises after a successful model call, it is not the issue. The real gap: the fence is only in `prepare_model_attempt`, keyed by `task_ref+purpose`; `RuntimeArchiveTransport` passes `task_ref=self.request_ref`, so two different archive questions for the same request_ref share one attempt fence (acceptable), but a retried call with a different `request_ref` for the same underlying provider operation will egress again since operation_ref derives from `request_ref+binding_digest` and is not fenced across request_refs. Meanwhile the durable attempt record stores `input_digest` but never compares it on reuse.
findings.fix: Store and compare input_digest on ModelAttemptAlreadyRecorded to distinguish identical-retry from divergent-replay, and fence on the provider operation_ref in addition to task_ref so distinct request_ref values cannot replay the same archive content.

findings.title: Cancellation/deadline handling not visible; guard only checked pre-send
findings.issue: The guard is invoked once immediately before building the request inside `transport()`, which is called under `execute_reserved_groups`. If cancellation occurs after the guard check but before/during `response.read`, the call still proceeds and the durable attempt is already recorded, so a cancelled task cannot be resumed and the spend is not prevented. The project requires durable no-replay/cancellation; there is no second guard check before recording usage or returning.
findings.fix: Invoke the guard again after response receipt and before returning the receipt/usage, and record cancellation state durably so a cancelled attempt is not silently completed.

findings.title: max_tokens unvalidated against provider bounds
findings.issue: `max_tokens=1000` is passed straight through to `complete_with_receipt` with no validation or clamping; `ScopedModelClient` does not check max_tokens either, only body size. A caller with a larger value could exceed intended cost bounds (though usage is capped at 1,000,000 tokens in validation).
findings.fix: Validate `max_tokens` is an int within an explicit bounded range in `complete_with_receipt` before building the request body.

findings.title: History content-length not individually bounded before body assembly
findings.issue: History items are copied with only role/content-type validation; individual content size is not bounded until the whole body exceeds 48000 bytes, which is enforced after JSON serialization. This is fail-closed overall but allows large string allocations before rejection.
findings.fix: Bound each history item's content length explicitly during validation.

findings.summary: Within the supplied archive/model/model-attempt modules the transport enforces immutable provenance, explicit paired grants (query + separate context scope for non-OpenAI providers), redirect denial, body/response bounds, and a durable one-shot attempt fence keyed on task_ref+purpose that forbids automatic retry after unknown outcomes, and the provided tests exercise real HTTP, revocation, provider-scoped group separation, and unknown-outcome no-replay. However, the attempt fence stores input_digest without ever comparing it on reuse, so a divergent retry under a different request_ref can replay the same provider content, and cancellation is only checked once pre-send so a cancelled task may complete and spend, both inconsistent with durable no-replay/cancellation requirements. Additional smaller gaps are unvalidated max_tokens and late body-size enforcement. Because several core modules (capabilities registry, composition, synthesis, deletion, fixtures) were not supplied, grant-boundary, citation, and unknown-pricing behavior could not be independently verified.
